figures.title: Figure 1
figures.llm_description: (a) Schematics showing the splitting of the two spin-polarized bands (parabolic bands with different colors) in the Rashba effect. (b) Top view of the spin textures at the energy contours shown in panel a. (c) Illustration of (left) type-I and (right) type-II Weyl semimetals (WSMs). (d) Schematic phase diagram showing topologically distinct phases of the Pb1−xSnxTe alloy with the variation of two parameters, polarity and Sn/Pb ratio. Panel adapted from Reference 102.

figures.title: Figure 2
figures.llm_description: Ferroelectric metal WTe2. (a) Schematic illustration of the three equivalent distortion vectors for the polarization up states, P1up, P2up, and P3up (solid lines) and the polarization down states, P1down, P2down, and P3down (dashed lines). The curved arrows denote low-energy transitions between polarization up and down states along different distortion vectors; switching between up and down polarization along the same distortion vector has a prohibitively high energy barrier. Panel adapted from

figures.title: Figure 3
figures.llm_description: Geometric polar metals. In Ca3Ru2O7, the combined (a) zone-boundary rotation and (b) tilt modes couple to (c) the zone-center polar mode to cause the polar symmetry. (d) The polar Pm21n structure of Bi5Mn5O17, depicting the displacements of the Bi atoms (blue arrows) that result in a net polarization P along the b direction. Panels a–c adapted with permission from Reference 55; copyright 2018 American Chemical Society. Panel d adapted from Reference 18.
